title: How to change cursor in Pages on Mac: system settings and visibility tips explained
metaTitle: How to change cursor on Mac in Pages
description: Learn how to change cursor on Mac settings to improve visibility in Apple Pages. Discover system-wide adjustments and workarounds for your text insertion point.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: You cannot change the text insertion cursor shape directly within the Apple Pages application on your Mac. You can, however, adjust your system-wide mouse pointer settings in macOS to improve visibility across all apps.
tldr: Pages does not have internal settings for the text insertion cursor.
Change the system-wide mouse pointer via System Settings.
Use the Shake mouse pointer to locate feature for better visibility.
Adjust your macOS Accent Color to change the highlight and cursor tint.
Keyboard shortcuts are your best tool for finding the insertion point.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor in Pages

Many users want to customize their workflow. A common request is changing the blinking vertical line that marks where your text appears. Apple keeps the Pages interface clean and consistent. There is no menu option to swap this line for a different shape or color. This design choice prevents visual clutter in your documents. It also ensures that your text remains readable regardless of the font or size you choose.
How to change cursor on Mac system settings

While the text cursor itself is fixed, the mouse pointer is fully adjustable. These changes affect your entire Mac. They help you find your place when you move from the document to the toolbar or menus.

items: Open the Apple Menu () and select System Settings.
Navigate to Accessibility in the sidebar.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to make the arrow easier to see.
Click the color wells for Pointer outline color and Pointer fill color to customize your look.

blocks.text: Using keyboard navigation to find your cursor

If you lose track of your insertion point in a long paragraph, keyboard shortcuts are faster than searching with your eyes. Hold the Shift key and tap the left or right arrow. This highlights the character next to your cursor. The highlight color makes the location of your cursor obvious. Press the opposite arrow to clear the selection once you have found your spot.
Managing cursor visibility with Accent Colors

The color of your selection and insertion point often matches your system Accent Color. If you have trouble seeing the cursor against a white background, try a darker or more vibrant accent color. Go to System Settings, then Appearance. Choose a different color from the list. This change might require a restart of Pages to take full effect in your document.
Common mistakes when customizing your cursor

Some users download third-party apps to force custom cursor shapes. This often causes problems. These apps can conflict with macOS accessibility features. They may cause the cursor to flicker or disappear during typing. Stick to native macOS settings to keep your experience stable. Avoid apps that modify private system files.

faq.question: Can I change the blinking cursor to a block shape in Pages?
faq.answer: No, Pages does not support changing the text insertion cursor shape. It is always a vertical line.

faq.question: Does changing the mouse pointer size affect the text cursor?
faq.answer: No, the accessibility settings for the mouse pointer only affect the arrow cursor, not the text insertion point.

faq.question: Why is my cursor invisible in my document?
faq.answer: This usually happens if your text color or background color is too similar to the cursor color. Try changing your system Accent Color or adjusting your document background.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner of your screen and choose System Settings.

steps.name: Access Accessibility
steps.text: Scroll down the sidebar and click on Accessibility to view your display options.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer
steps.text: Click on Display and use the sliders to increase your pointer size or change its color.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor is hard to see against text
troubleshooting.fix: Change your system Accent Color in System Settings > Appearance.
Uninstall the third-party app and restart your Mac.
